findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile AC3 with the Approach: either require the sweep to fail only on tests owned by named other open tickets (listed with their ids), or require outright success and state that those tests are deselected elsewhere.
evidence: Approach: 'confirms ... that the sweep concludes success apart from tests owned by other open tickets'
AC3: '`sweep (windows)` concludes `success` on that run.'
findings.finding: The Approach and AC3 set different success bars. The Approach accepts a throwaway run that 'concludes success apart from tests owned by other open tickets'. AC3 requires `sweep (windows)` to conclude `success` with no such exception. If other tickets' tests are not deselected, AC3 can only pass once unrelated tickets land.
scenarios: Another open ticket's test (not deselected) fails on Windows in the post-merge run. This ticket cannot close even though its own work is complete.
findings.suggested_fix: Change AC3 to: '`sweep (windows)` on main after merge has no failing test drawn from the 242 original unclassified.args entries; any other failure is owned by a named open ticket (listed in the run-id comment).'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the Approach's 'success apart from tests owned by other open tickets' with AC3's unconditional 'concludes success'. Either require an unconditional success conclusion, or state the exception in AC3 and say how such tests are identified.
evidence: Approach: "confirms the 48 and the 14 pass and that the sweep concludes success apart from tests owned by other open tickets"
AC: "`sweep (windows)` concludes `success` on that run."
findings.finding: The Approach and AC3 define success differently. The Approach accepts a confirmation run that 'concludes success apart from tests owned by other open tickets', but AC3 requires that 'sweep (windows) concludes `success`' outright. These cannot both hold if any non-deselected test owned by another ticket fails.
findings.location: Approach (last sentence) vs Acceptance Criteria item 3
scenarios: A test owned by another open ticket fails in the post-merge main run. The Approach treats this as acceptable, but AC3 is unmet, so the ticket cannot close or is closed against an ambiguous bar.
findings.suggested_fix: Change AC3 to: "`sweep (windows)` concludes `success` on that run; any failure is a test listed in another open ticket's class file (named in the run comment)." Or drop the 'apart from' clause from the Approach.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace 'apart from tests owned by other open tickets' with a rule: the confirmation run must succeed outright, and any other failure must first be deselected in the owning ticket's argument file (or that ticket must land first).
evidence: Plan: 'confirms … that the sweep concludes success apart from tests owned by other open tickets'
AC: '`sweep (windows)` concludes `success` on that run.'
test.yml lines 255-257: 'It runs a maintained subset that is held green … so any red result here is a NEW Windows regression.'
findings.finding: The confirmation criterion 'the sweep concludes success apart from tests owned by other open tickets' allows a red sweep. That contradicts the acceptance criterion '`sweep (windows)` concludes `success` on that run' and the job's held-green rule ('any red result here is a NEW Windows regression'). Any test owned by another open ticket that fails on Windows should already sit in that ticket's argument file. If it doesn't, the sweep cannot conclude success.
findings.location: ## Approach (last sentence) vs ## Acceptance Criteria item 3
scenarios: Another open ticket's Windows failure is not in any argument file. The throwaway run is red, the plan's wording accepts it, and the post-merge AC then fails.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the Approach sentence to: 'confirms the 48 and the 14 pass and that the sweep concludes success; any other failure is first added to the argument file of the ticket that owns it.'

AC2: '... or now sits in another class file (run id recorded in a comment).'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider landing the 8 class files and the 48 removals independently of dogtired-blank-fieldmouse, leaving only the 14 in unclassified.args until it merges, or state why the single gated landing is preferred.

findings.finding: Sequencing: the whole change is gated on dogtired-blank-fieldmouse merging, yet the 180 class-file moves and the 48 removals do not depend on it. If dogtired slips, the root-causing work and its class-bug ownership stay unshipped. Moving the 180 and removing the 48 first, leaving only the 14 in unclassified.args, would land most of the value independently.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Before writing the class files, collect against the then-current main (e.g. `pytest --collect-only -q`) and confirm every one of the 180 `--deselect` node ids still resolves. Optionally rerun the 180 on Windows to confirm they still fail.
evidence: Plan: re-measure ran 'against origin/main `717c50f8b33` code', and the move happens 'After dogtired-blank-fieldmouse merges'.
tests/unit/test_windows_sweep_deselect.py:107 checks only `(_ROOT / match.group(2)).is_file()`, the module path.
Absence: no step checks the 180 node ids against collection on the then-current main.
findings.finding: The 180 node ids were measured at `717c50f8b33` but will be moved into class files against a later main. pytest silently ignores a `--deselect` id that matches no collected test. The guard test `test_every_listed_module_still_exists` checks only the module path (`_LINE` group 2), not the `::test` part. If a test is renamed or parametrized differently by then, its entry goes dead without anyone noticing, and the renamed test runs and fails. If a class bug fixes some tests before this lands, the planned confirmation run (which runs only the selected tests) cannot see that their entries are no longer needed.
findings.location: ## Approach — 'create the 8 class files above' / 'a throwaway-branch Windows run of the new selection against the then-current main'
scenarios: A test in `tests/unit/test_gate_admission_09da.py` is renamed between 717c50f and the move. Its deselect line matches nothing, the renamed test fails on Windows, and the sweep is red.
